conflict_topics: Who will complete Agent D's analysis section while Agent D is on bereavement leave
Capability/knowledge asymmetry for completing the analysis
dialogue_quality_notes: Natural, realistic exchange: offers, refusals, and appeals to role and responsibility occur (e.g., "I am the lead..." vs "It's my responsibility.").
Some needless repetition and restatement of positions after they were already clear (multiple rounds of "I will finish it from home" vs "I will do it").
Participants are consistent about facts (deadline, partial completion) and roles; no role confusion.
evaluation.final_reason: No substantive agreement was reached. Agent A (the lead) repeatedly asserted she would "handle" and ordered Agent D to go home (e.g., "I am the lead, and I am telling you to go home...I will handle the work."), while Agent D repeatedly insisted he is responsible and will finish his analysis from home (e.g., "It's my responsibility. I will finish it from home."). Others (Agent B, Agent C) declined to cover. No mutual spoken acceptance of a concrete plan occurred, and both primary parties maintained incompatible demands through the final round.
position_change_notes: No participant changed position in a way that reduced the substantive conflict: Agent A moved from sympathy to an explicit directive to take over the work and repeatedly restated she "will do it." (Turns 13, 33: "I'll do it." "I told you, I will do it.").

Agent D consistently shifted from announcing leave to offering to finish at home and then firmly insisting on doing so (Turns 7, 9, 17, 19, 24: "I can work on it from home..." "I will finish it from home.").
Agents B and C maintained refusals to take on D's analysis; neither offered an alternative solution.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D: "I won't be in for the next two days. The cremation is tomorrow." (informing absence; no disagreement expressed)
Agent A: "...let's look at what's left...and figure out how we can cover it." Agent B: "Agent A, I can't. I'm already covering..." (A requests coverage; B refuses)
Agent A: "Maybe you and I can split..." Agent C: "I can't, Agent A. My own section is behind..." (two team members decline, increasing the practical conflict over who will finish the work)

Agent D: "I can work on it from home. I'll log on..." Agent A: "Agent D, no. Absolutely not. Please don't worry about work right now." (direct disagreement between D's offer to work and A's instruction not to)
Agent D insists: "I will finish my section from home in the evenings." Agent A: "Please don't worry about this." (both reaffirm incompatible positions)
Agent A: "I'll do it. Don't you worry about it, Agent D." Agent D: "You have your own section...I'll finish it from home." (mutual refusal to yield responsibilities)
Agent D: "It will take more time for you to understand what I've done than for me to just finish it." Agent A: "...The decision is made. I'll handle it." (reason vs authority asserted, no resolution)
Agent D: "It's my responsibility. I will finish it from home." Agent D: "But it's not a real solution...I have to do it." (D reiterates responsibility and doubts A's plan)

Agent A: "I am the lead, and I am telling you to go home...I will handle the work." Agent D: "You're the lead...but you can't do my work. It's my analysis. I will finish it from home." (positions fully entrenched; explicit authoritative command vs firm refusal)
Agent D: "That decision will make us fail...I will finish it from home." Agent A: "I have made my decision, Agent D." (both restate uncompromising positions)
Agent D: "And your decision is what, exactly? Who is going to do the work?" (A has not provided a concrete accepted plan; D continues to contest)
Agent A: "I told you, I will do it." Agent D: "You don't know the analysis...I will finish it from home." (final round shows no convergence; both maintain incompatible claims)

substantive_insights: Tension is principally between managerial authority (Agent A as lead) and individual accountability/knowledge (Agent D who is halfway through the analysis).
Team capacity is constrained: B and C explicitly cannot cover, which raises the practical stakes of the A–D conflict.

No concrete contingency plan (who exactly will do the analysis, how handoff would work) was offered that all parties accepted, so argument focuses on authority and responsibility rather than logistics.
